The question focuses on evolutionary adaptations in respiratory systems. Amphibians rely on cutaneous respiration and gills (in larval stages) in addition to primitive lungs, so they still require supplementary gas exchange. Mammals have well-developed lungs but evolved later. Trematoda (flatworms) lack specialized respiratory organs entirely and use diffusion. Reptiles were the first group to evolve lungs with extensive internal folding (alveoli-like structures), allowing efficient gas exchange without needing supplemental organs like amphibian skin or gills.  

Final answer: (B)
